**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind lane results to their catalog actors**

When candidate output is model-controlled or a producer is misconfigured, admission checks only that the claimed lane keyword is required; it never matches `:evidence/producer` or its revisions against that lane's catalog profile. Because `aggregate-verdict` receives no catalog at all, one arbitrary syntactically valid producer can claim every required lane and supply accepted blockers or complete results, defeating the dedicated-actor authority boundary. Validate each result against the selected lane profile before accepting it.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L9-L11](https://github.com/open-hax/eta-mu/blob/847079d85578ccc7bc07543e40e8fdf8ca1b9f13/AGENTS.md#L9-L11)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match retained artifact references, not only hashes**

When a finding reuses an inspected artifact's hash but supplies a different `:artifact/kind` or `:artifact/location`, this hash-only membership check admits it as retained. The fabricated reference can then support a confirmed blocker and appear in the aggregate even though that cited reference was never in the lane's inspected manifest; compare against the retained artifact references themselves or derive citation metadata from the manifest.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L9-L11](https://github.com/open-hax/eta-mu/blob/847079d85578ccc7bc07543e40e8fdf8ca1b9f13/AGENTS.md#L9-L11)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject artifacts outside the selected lane's catalog**

When an otherwise valid lane result places an arbitrary artifact kind in `:coverage/inspected` and cites that exact reference, admission never compares the artifact's kind with the resolved profile's `:lane/artifact-kinds`. A contracts/schema producer can therefore use test, CI, or fabricated artifact classes to support an accepted confirmed blocker, bypassing the catalog's dedicated evidence-class boundary; validate every inspected reference against the selected lane profile.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L9-L11](https://github.com/open-hax/eta-mu/blob/8c27f2ddda691074e14982780a3f90922f804842/AGENTS.md#L9-L11)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass an admissible catalog to verdict tests**

Every aggregation test passes the `required-lanes` set as argument two, but `aggregate-verdict` now requires a catalog and immediately runs `catalog-admissibility-errors` on it. The first test therefore throws `Invalid evidence lane catalog` before reaching any assertion, and the same mismatch affects every later call; update these tests and their lane-result fixtures to use the catalog-bound API.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L81-L83](https://github.com/open-hax/eta-mu/blob/8c27f2ddda691074e14982780a3f90922f804842/AGENTS.md#L81-L83)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read actor identities from the producer profile**

The catalog stores actors at `[:lane/producer :producer/actor]`, so mapping `:lane/actor` returns `[nil nil nil]` and this newly added uniqueness assertion always fails. The later shared-actor fixture uses the same obsolete path and consequently produces an invalid closed catalog rather than the expected shared-actor error; update both accesses to the nested producer field.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L81-L83](https://github.com/open-hax/eta-mu/blob/8c27f2ddda691074e14982780a3f90922f804842/AGENTS.md#L81-L83)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce each lane's maximum finding budget**

When a producer returns more findings than its catalog profile's `:max-findings`, this admission path only validates each finding individually and accepts the unbounded vector. That makes the advertised hard output bound non-enforcing and allows model-controlled results to exceed the 20/25-finding limits before aggregation; reject results whose finding count exceeds the selected lane budget.

💡 Result:

In ClojureScript 1.11.60, the mapv function is designed to take one or more collections and return a vector containing the results of applying a function f to the items of those collections [1]. Regarding the handling of collections and ISeq: 1. Compatibility with Non-Sequential Collections: The mapv function accepts any collection that can be treated as a sequence [1]. When you pass a collection to mapv, it is processed via its sequence representation (using protocols such as ISeq) [2]. Therefore, while mapv is intended to return a vector, it is flexible regarding the input type, as long as the input satisfies the requirements to be traversed as a sequence [1]. 2. Implementation Details: The internal implementation of mapv, as shown in the ClojureScript core library, utilizes reduce (or delegates to map for multiple collections) to construct the resulting vector [1]. Specifically, for a single collection, it uses a transient vector to efficiently build the result: (defn mapv ([f coll] (-> (reduce (fn [v o] (conj! v (f o))) (transient []) coll) persistent!))...) Because mapv processes input as a sequence, it does not require the input to be a specific sequential type (like a vector) to function, but it will always produce a vector as its output [1][2].

If you are seeing an error related to missing sequence support, it is likely because you are passing an unsupported type to a function that expects a sequence (such as `map`, `first`, or `rest`). To resolve this, you have a few options depending on your goal: 1. **Return after a shape-validation failure.**

If `:catalog/lanes` is `0`, `mapv` and `mapcat` traverse it before the `shape-valid?` branches run. The invalid catalog can therefore throw instead of returning `:invalid-catalog-shape`. Move all lane traversal into the valid-shape branch and add a regression assertion for `(catalog-admissibility-errors {:catalog/lanes 0})`.

Line 16: `(mapv :lane/actor lanes)` — the `lane-profile-schema` defines `:lane/producer` (a map), not `:lane/actor`. Every element is nil, `(count [nil nil nil])` = `(count (distinct [nil nil nil]))` = 3, so the test passes without verifying actor uniqueness. The same wrong key appears in the `duplicate-or-shared-lanes-fail-admission` test at lines 36-37 where `(:lane/actor first-lane)` is also nil, making `shared-actor` an assoc on a nil path. Fix: replace `(:lane/actor lanes)` with `(mapv #(get-in % [:lane/producer :producer/actor]) lanes)` and adjust the shared-actor test to use the correct key path.

The lane-result helper constructs `:evidence/producer` as `{:producer/actor-binding ... :producer/profile-revision ... :producer/workflow-revision ... :producer/attestation-hash ...}` — missing `:producer/actor`. The `producer-schema` (law/evidence_review.cljs line 41-47) has `:producer/actor` as a required, non-optional key. `valid-lane-result-shape?` would return false for every test-generated lane-result. This compounds with finding test-wrong-arg-type-1: even if the catalog argument were correct, lane results would be rejected. Fix: add `:producer/actor :eta-mu.agent/<lane>-reviewer` to the helper's producer map.

`aggregate-verdict` signature is `[snapshot catalog lane-results]`. The test calls `(review/aggregate-verdict snapshot required-lanes results)` where `required-lanes` is `#{:contracts-schema :tests-failures :ci-provenance}` (a set). Inside `aggregate-verdict`, `(:catalog/required-lanes #{...})` returns nil, then `(lane-catalog/catalog-admissibility-errors #{...})` validates a set against the catalog schema — the set lacks `:catalog/lanes` so `(:catalog/lanes #{...})` is nil, `lanes` is nil, `empty?` returns true, and the function returns `[:empty-lane-catalog]`, causing the `throw` on line 214. This affects every test in the file (lines 76, 85-88, 102-104, 120-123, 136, 146-147, 151-152, 175-178, 187). The tests cannot pass as written. Fix: construct a catalog map with `:catalog/version 1`, `:catalog/id`, `:catalog/required-lanes required-lanes`, and `:catalog/lanes` with lane profiles matching the test data.
